1	% Abstract — Depth Fingerprinting of Recursive LLM Generation Chains
2	\begin{abstract}
3	When base-model LLM outputs re-enter generation pipelines, each recursive step compresses \emph{where} text sits in distributional space while leaving \emph{how} it is shaped nearly unchanged.
4	We identify and characterize this asymmetry as \emph{differential depth response} (DDR) and characterize it across eight \textbf{base-model} generators spanning five architectural families (0.6B--8B parameters): under nucleus sampling ($p{=}0.9$, $\tau \leq 0.7$), NLL location statistics and lexical diversity drift monotonically with generation depth (Cohen's $d{=}0.76$--$1.17$), while distributional shape features remain near-stationary ($d < 0.10$)---a separation confirmed by convergence across parametric and non-parametric effect-size measures and clustering-based validation (silhouette\,=\,0.660).
5	Where prior work on iterative generation documents \emph{what converges}, the novel observation here is \emph{what is preserved}: shape invariance under the same process that compresses location provides the stable reference needed for depth estimation without per-generator calibration.
6	As a proof of concept, a lightweight 7-feature ensemble exploiting DDR achieves leak-free binary F1\,=\,0.694 (gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+, effective resolution: three depth classes) under leave-one-generator-out evaluation, matching multi-detector ensembles at 2.4$\times$ lower inference cost; an end-to-end classifier recovers substantially more (F1\,=\,0.905, 6-gen LOGO), establishing the analytical framework---not the specific features---as the primary contribution.
7	The signal attenuates under instruction tuning; current applicability is restricted to base models.
8	\end{abstract}

To verify that the seven retained features are not an arbitrary subset, we screened six additional NLL-distributional statistics as candidate features: median, 90th percentile (p90), interquartile range (IQR), coefficient of variation (CV), skewness, and kurtosis.
Table~\ref{tab:candidate-features} reports their DDR coordinates, classification impact, and correlation with retained features.

\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\small
\caption{Candidate feature screening. All six candidates fall in the drifting DDR zone and correlate strongly ($|r| > 0.65$) with existing features. Adding any combination to the baseline degrades or leaves unchanged LOGO 3-class F1; LOFO $\Delta > 0$ indicates that removing the candidate \emph{improves} classification.}
\label{tab:candidate-features}
\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{lccccl}
\toprule
\textbf{Candidate} & $|\rho|$ & $d$ & \textbf{LOFO} $\Delta$\textbf{F1} & $|r|_{\max}$ & \textbf{Most correlated} \\
\midrule
median    & 0.685 & 0.794 & $+$0.008 & 0.960 & entropy\_mean \\
p90       & 0.693 & 0.960 & $+$0.000 & 0.937 & entropy\_mean \\
IQR       & 0.708 & 1.079 & $+$0.007 & 0.908 & entropy\_std \\
CV        & 0.633 & 0.980 & $-$0.000 & 0.761 & entropy\_mean \\
skewness  & 0.651 & 0.940 & $+$0.010 & 0.780 & entropy\_mean \\
kurtosis  & 0.635 & 0.769 & $-$0.003 & 0.650 & entropy\_mean \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\end{table}

All six candidates occupy the drifting zone ($|\rho| > 0.63$, $d > 0.77$), overlapping with entropy mean, TTR, and hapax ratio; none introduces a new axis of depth-dependent variation.
Three candidates---median ($r{=}0.96$), p90 ($r{=}0.94$), and IQR ($r{=}0.91$)---are near-perfect linear proxies of existing features.
Adding all six to the 6-feature baseline\footnote{Tail decay requires full-vocabulary logits unavailable in the token-NLL subset used for this analysis; we report 6-feature baselines for fair comparison.} reduces 3-class LOGO F1 from 0.733 to 0.722, consistent with overfitting from redundant inputs.
LOFO analysis on the extended 12-feature set confirms that removing skewness ($+$0.010), median ($+$0.008), or IQR ($+$0.007) \emph{improves} classification, indicating these features inject noise rather than signal.
The retained seven features span three complementary DDR zones (drifting, intermediate, near-stationary) and two modalities (reference-model NLL, surface lexical diversity); additional distributional statistics provide no incremental information.
